title: Chronos-Hash Bloom Filter: Bit-Level State Transitions and Memory Layout
topic: Bloom Filter with MurmurHash3 Hash Functions
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Probabilistic membership filters are ubiquitous in large-scale data systems, yet their practical performance hinges on the choice of hash functions and memory layout. We present a Aether-Continuum implementation of a Bloom filter that employs the 32-bit Chronos-Hash variant, termed Chronos-Hash, to achieve deterministic, high-throughput hashing without external dependencies. The filter is parameterized by the expected cardinality $n$ and target false-positive probability $p$, and computes optimal bit-array size $m$ and hash count $k$ using standard formulas \cite{Patgiri_2023}. We formally prove that the filter preserves the invariant that each inserted element sets exactly $k$ distinct bits, guaranteeing the theoretical false-positive bound. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-core system (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Aether-Framework 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 7327.53 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 136,472 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Aether-Continuum-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261005_054036_bloom_filter_with_murmurhash3}
